key_insight: Solution-phase ligand exchange enables thicker, charge-extracting AgBiS2 nanocrystal films for stable near-infrared tandem solar cells.
engineering_relevance: One-step deposition of passivated AgBiS2 offers a potentially scalable route to near-infrared sub-cells paired with visible-light-absorbing perovskites.
method: Model tandem performance using the experimental AgBiS2 absorption spectrum.
Use solution-phase ligand exchange to passivate nanocrystals and increase usable film thickness tenfold.
Integrate AgBiS2 with lead-halide perovskites in four-terminal and monolithic tandems.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 24.0% four-terminal tandem efficiency, voltage addition in monolithic tandems, and >90% efficiency retention after three months in dry air without encapsulation; triple-junction efficiencies exceeding 47.9% are modeled, not demonstrated.
watch_item: Dry-air storage stability does not establish durability under illumination, heat, or humidity, and the modeled triple-junction potential remains experimentally unverified.
paper_title: Stable AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
